heading: INT. SMALL-TOWN LIBRARY - READING ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. SMALL-TOWN LIBRARY - READING ROOM - DAY
Oak tables.
Green banker's lamps.
Dust turning in a slant of window light.
MRS. HARGROVE, 70s, in a cardigan buttoned wrong, sits at a long table with a stack of postcards in front of her, writing one with trembling care.
Opposite, LEO, 12, elbows on the wood, pretends to read.
She finishes a line.
He pretends to turn a page.
She sets the pen down, and he sets down the book, and they watch each other across the sunlit table.
You've been writing the same card for an hour.
units.name: LEO

units.text: It's a difficult card.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE

units.text: Who's it for?
units.name: LEO

units.text: My husband.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE

units.text: Is he away?
units.name: LEO

units.text: For some years.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE

units.text: He nods, as if this were an ordinary answer.
She slides the card across.
Read it.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE

units.text: He reads aloud, haltingly.
"Dear Harold. The roses are in. I'm well. I miss the sound of you coming up the stairs."
units.name: LEO

units.text: He looks up.
She keeps her eyes on the lamp.
That's nice.
units.name: LEO

units.text: It's a lie. I'm not well.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE

units.text: The door opens.
DENISE FAIRLEY, 40s, in a county social worker's lanyard, breathless from the stairs, stops in the doorway with a clipboard against her chest.
Mrs. Hargrove? I'm so sorry I'm late.
units.name: DENISE

units.text: Mrs. Hargrove straightens.
Collects the postcards with quick, practiced hands and slides them into her handbag.
Leo stands.
Leo, this is Denise. She'll be driving me home.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE

units.text: Is she your daughter?
units.name: LEO

units.text: No, sweetheart. I'm just a friend.
units.name: DENISE

units.text: A new one. They come and go.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE

units.text: Leo hesitates.
Then holds out the card, the one in his hand, the one with the lie.
You forgot this.
units.name: LEO

units.text: She takes it.
Looks at it a long moment, folds it once, and tucks it into his shirt pocket.
Keep it. Someone should believe me.
units.name: MRS. HARGROVE
